captions: This image shows an mature MII-oocyte with an enlarged perivitelline space. Moderate debris is visible all around the perivitelline space. The first polar body is close to the 6-o clock position . The zona pellucida appears normal.
This image shows an oocyte. There is granulation visible in the whole perivitelline space. The perivitilline space is enlarged. The oocyte has 2 polar bodies, that are not right next to each other.

This picture shows a zygote with the two pronuclei in the center. Both pronuclei are in the process of fading. One polar body is detached from the zygote. The perivitelline space is large and show lots of debris. The zona pellucida is normal.
This is a 2-cell embryo. The lower cell is clearly smaller than the other one. Slight granules are visible in the perivitelline space.
This picture shows a six-cell embryo with blastomeres of unequal size. Fragmentation is moderate. The zona pellucida is relatively thin.

This image shows a cleavage-stage embryo with approximately 8-9 blastomeres. The blastomeres differ in size and several cytoplasmic fragments are visible, suggesting a moderate fragmentation. The zona pellucida is uniform.
This is a 8 cell embryo with fragmentation in the lower part of the embryo. The zona pellucida appears thickened. The blastomere on the top shows an interphase nucleus.

This image shows a mature metaphase II oocyte, as indicated by the presence of a clearly visible first polar body. The ooplasm is homogenous with a small vacuole in the center. The zona pellucida is uniform.
This is a four -cell embryo not being stage-appropriate. There are three different cell sizes. Moderate fragmentation can be seen. The zona pellucida is normal.

This embryo has 6 blastomeres. The blastomeres vary in size. The largest blastomere shows a very inhomogeneous cytoplasm. The embryo shows slight fragmentation. The zona appears a little denser than a regular one.
This is a 8-cell embryo with unevenly-sized blastomeres. There are some fragments between the blastomeres.
This image shows a cleavage-stage day 3 embryo with approximately 8-9 blastomeres. The blastomeres are unequal in size. Moderate fragmentation is visible. The zona pellucida is uniform.
This image shows a day 3 embryo with approximately 9 blastomeres. The blastomeres are showing stage-specific partially asymmetry in size. Fragmentation is visible. The zona pellucida is uniform.

This picture shows a full blastocyst of Gardner grade 3. The zona pellucida is not thinned yet. The inner cell mass is not fully compacted (quality B). The trophectoderm is also of quality B. The overall quality of the blastocyst is 3BB according to Gardner criteria.
There is no embryo in this picture.
In this image there is neither an oocyte nor an embryo visible. There are some fibers or plastic particles visible.
This image shows an oocyte with a pronucleus-like structure slightly above the center of the oocyte. There are several inclusions in the ooplasm that vary in size and location.

This image shows a mature metaphase II oocyte. The first polar body is located at 9 o clock position. The ooplasm is homogeneous, mild cytoplasmic inclusions are visible. The zona pellucida is uniform.
This picture shows a regular two-cell embryo with minor fragmentation between the two blastomeres. The two blastomeres are of equal size. The zona pellucida is normal.
This picture shows a three-cell embryo with evenly-sized blastomeres. This dysmorphism is probably caused by trichotomous mitosis. The zona pellucida is regular.
